status: Needs review — measured live twice on 2026-10-21, including once after this note's own PR merged: the legacy Pages publisher served a 3.8-day-old board
finding: GitHub Pages for this repository is configured build_type 'legacy' with source 'main:/', so two publishers write to one URL: pages.yml deploys the verified artifact with actions/deploy-pages, and GitHub's own legacy builder publishes the committed root of main (the 2026-10-18 bootstrap fallback, revision 88b1b2c3, 98 rows). On 2026-10-21 the overwrite was observed directly rather than inferred. Two cache-busted reads of https://buffedlizard55-lab.github.io/MaltaProj4/build-info.json plus the Pages build API give this sequence: at ~20:11Z the live receipt was revision 47f230b, built 2026-10-21T19:57:45Z, 76 rows (the verified artifact); the legacy Pages build for commit 63f4172 completed at 20:12:40Z; at ~20:15Z the same URL returned revision 88b1b2c3, built 2026-10-18T00:52:19Z, 98 rows — the committed root fallback, 91.4 hours old, with June-dated rows and October-18 matches instead of the current board; pages.yml run 39668307571 finished deploying at 20:20:28Z (verify-build and deploy both successful) and the fresh artifact was served again. Stale window ≈8 minutes. The page was honest throughout: the deployed freshness strip read 'Snapshot is older than 8 hours: every percentage below is expired and must not be used as a current pick', and this session's auditor fails that state on purpose (research/harvest-93fafca6/ROOT-FALLBACK-AUDIT.md, 10 pass / 1 warn / 1 fail, exit 1). The fallback is also materially different data: 98 rows with 34 'open' June-dated scheduled entries Hotspawn never closed, against the live 75 rows with 13 open. No pick, probability or row value was changed by this finding; it is a publication-state irregularity. The same overwrite was observed a second time, independently, after PR #123 merged. At ~21:14Z the live receipt was revision fcaf608b (the merge commit), built 2026-10-21T21:10:18Z, 75 rows; at 21:14:24Z a runner reading the same URL got revision 88b1b2c3, built 2026-10-18T00:52:19Z, 98 rows, 92.37 h old; at 21:17:59Z the independent live audit reported 11 pass / 2 info / 1 warn / 2 fail, with live-board-fresh FAIL at 92.43 h and glance-completeness-fresh FAIL because 13 fixtures open at that minute had no row on the served board. Two reads of one URL 30 seconds apart returned two different boards. The mechanism is visible in the API and is worse than a coin flip: the legacy builder completed a build for EVERY push to main in the window (21:03:38Z fcaf608, 21:10:55Z b1adaa4, 21:11:31Z 87db124, 21:14:07Z 47c1b9d, 21:16:45Z 7148716), while two pages.yml runs on main concluded "cancelled" with ZERO jobs created and cancel_actor null — run 39676669813 (b1adaa4, created 21:10:57Z) and run 39677102451 (47c1b9d, created 21:14:08Z) — so those pushes never deployed an artifact and never overwrote the stale root build that had landed seconds earlier. pages.yml sets concurrency {group: cs2-scout-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: false}, so that setting did not cancel them; why GitHub cancelled two queued runs and recorded no actor is NOT established by these readings and is not asserted here. What is established is the consequence: with four merges in seven minutes, the publisher that runs scripts/verify_live.py before serving was dropped twice, and the publisher that serves a 3.8-day-old board with no check ran every time. Same shape as concurrent-pages-deploy-failure-2026-10-16, now with cancelled-run evidence attached.

status: Needs review — the one outstanding fix is the repository owner's, and both token types are provably refused
finding: Every session since 1abdd416 (PR #57) has named the same single fix for the dual-publisher race: set the Pages publishing source to GitHub Actions, which stops the legacy main:/ builder from republishing the committed root. It has never been applied, and until now the reason was not on the readable record — session c4d25599's explicitly pages:write-scoped attempt (run 38706399874) failed in 3 seconds and its log cannot be read from the authoring sandbox because the Actions log host is unreachable. This session reproduced the attempt twice and committed both raw responses. PUT https://api.github.com/repos/buffedlizard55-lab/MaltaProj4/pages with body {"build_type":"workflow"} returned HTTP 403 with body 'Resource not accessible by integration' from (a) the Arena integration token at 2026-10-21T20:20:18Z, request id C962:306C0:544D9:8CACF:6AD91E81, whose X-Oauth-Scopes header is empty, and (b) a workflow GITHUB_TOKEN with pages: write granted explicitly in .github/workflows/harvest-93fafca6.yml at 20:48:00Z, request id 780B:1EA56B:F5241B:31FA96A:6AD92502. Both responses carried X-Accepted-Github-Permissions: pages=write,administration=write, so the endpoint needs a token this repository's automation does not have. Owner action, one click and no code change: Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source → GitHub Actions. pages.yml's deploy job already uses actions/deploy-pages with pages: write and id-token: write and already verifies the served bytes against the build manifest, so workflow mode needs no other change; it only stops the second publisher. Until then the race is bounded by the next pages.yml run (≈8 minutes observed; four scheduled slots an hour at :04/:19/:34/:49 plus a 10-minute watchdog), and the site states its own staleness instead of hiding it. No setting was changed, bypassed or worked around by this session.

status: Needs review — dormant crash path in scripts/refresh.py::cache_bust, one-line fix, file owned by three active sessions so it is requested rather than edited
finding: urllib.parse.urlencode raises TypeError('not a valid non-string sequence or mapping object') when the first element of its sequence is a list rather than a tuple, and scripts/refresh.py::cache_bust builds its pairs with str.split('=', 1), which returns lists. Reproduced with the repository's own code: cache_bust('https://play.hotspawn.com/lobby', 'T1') returns 'https://play.hotspawn.com/lobby?_cb=T1', while cache_bust('https://play.hotspawn.com/lobby?tenantId=1', 'T1') raises TypeError. Impact today is none: Sources.bustable cache-busts only HTML on play.hotspawn.com (CACHE_BUST_HTML_HOSTS), the two lobby URLs carry no query string, so pairs is empty and [] + [tuple] begins with a tuple. It is therefore a latent crash path for any future cache-busted URL that carries arguments — and a refresh crash is the failure mode scripts/refresh.py's own header documents, where one blocked host cost eight open fixtures their roster lineups and dropped the board from 'every open row has a pick' to eight rows with no pick. The correct implementation already exists in this repository: scripts/cdn_probe_3c8d1136.py::bust builds tuples with [(k, v) for k, v in (pair.split('=', 1) for pair in ...)]. Suggested fix, one line in cache_bust: pairs = [tuple(pair.split('=', 1)) if '=' in pair else (pair, '') for pair in parts.query.split('&') if pair]. A regression test for the valueless-argument case is modelled in verification-93fafca6/test_audit_live.py::test_cache_bust_survives_a_valueless_argument, and this session's own copy of the helper uses tuples. scripts/refresh.py is claimed by sessions 2d0a85f2, 1395f539 and db1f35c5, so per the board rules the fix is logged as a cross-session request in COORDINATION.md instead of being applied here.
